source: JD 14 Nov 2026: online agents cost real money per token - 'it's not a charity'. Codex spent 25.6M tokens on 9 Nov, 14.5M on 10 Nov and 11.2M on 11 Nov, then ran out and could no longer advise or check anything. HB manages each online agent's budget; JD sets the numbers here.
meaning: A token is a piece of a word. Every token an online agent reads (its instructions, the files and records it opens, the conversation) and writes is paid for by JD. Reading a big file costs as much as writing it. When the day's budget is used up, the agent cannot advise or check anything until the next day.

copilot-instructor.note: GitHub Copilot in VS Code runs on JD's Copilot subscription; HB cannot see its token use, so it keeps to the same habits.

habits: Be brief: answer in as few words as the question needs; no restating the question, no long summaries of what you read.
Read only what you need: search first (grep_repo, knowledge_search), then open the exact lines; never re-read a file you already read in this turn.
One good answer beats several partial ones: no tool loops, no repeated checks of the same thing.
If the task is local work (running, editing, testing), say so and leave it to APEX and the local models - they cost nothing per token.
